History
Camp Courtney was opened as a U.S.
Marine Base in January 1956, when select units of the 3rd Marine Division were transferred there from Camp McGill in Yokosuka, Kanagawa, Japan.
Initially the base was called by its original name, Camp Tengan.
The first Marine units occupied Quonset huts, Nissen huts and Butler buildings.

Most of the huts were "strong-backed", which means they had concrete or concrete block ends, with cables strung over them at intervals whose ends were anchored in the ground in concrete, and had wooden hurricane shutters over the windows.
